name: Progressive Familial Heart Block Type I
aliases: Familial Progressive Atrioventricular Block Type I

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Progressive Familial Heart Block Type I

criteria.description: Progressive atrioventricular conduction block documented on ECG
Positive family history of conduction system disease or sudden cardiac death
Identification of pathogenic mutation in TRPM4 gene or other associated genes
Exclusion of other causes of atrioventricular block such as ischemic heart disease or myocarditis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive atrioventricular block with positive family history; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is helpful but not mandatory; diagnosis relies primarily on clinical and ECG findings with family history.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Syncope due to high-grade heart block

occasional.notes: May occur in advanced disease stages

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to cerebral hypoperfusion

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers
imaging: ECG showing progressive atrioventricular block (Mobitz type I or II, or complete heart block)
Holter monitoring demonstrating intermittent conduction abnormalities
Echocardiogram usually normal or mild structural changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TRPM4 gene commonly identified
Other associated gene mutations may be found in familial cases
other: Family pedigree analysis showing autosomal dominant inheritance
Response to pacemaker implantation in symptomatic patients

distinguishingFeatures: Idiopathic fibrosis of conduction system without family history
History of myocardial infarction or coronary artery disease
Regional wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram
Elevated cardiac biomarkers during acute events
Recent viral illness or systemic symptoms

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained sudden death in family
Progression to complete heart block with bradycardia
references: Andersen P, et al. Progressive familial heart block type I: clinical and genetic features. Heart Rhythm. 2019;16(3):456-463.
